paragraphs.text: Vitelliform macular dystrophies are inherited retinal dystrophies in which round, yellow deposits are seen on fundus examination. They include juvenile Best macular dystrophy and adult-onset vitelliform macular dystrophy (Manes et al., 2013). In IMPG1-related VMD, onset is usually in adulthood and visual impairment is moderate. Drusen-like lesions may lie next to the vitelliform deposits, the vitelliform material sits above a well-preserved retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), and the electrooculogram (EOG) is usually normal or only borderline (Manes et al., 2013; Meunier et al., 2014). Inheritance can be autosomal dominant or autosomal recessive (Manes et al., 2013), and onset in early childhood has been reported (Brandl et al., 2017).

paragraphs.text: Meunier et al. (2014) described 13 patients: 11 patients from 3 families with IMPG1 mutations and 2 patients from 1 family with an IMPG2 mutation. Onset was late and visual impairment was moderate, with a mean visual acuity of 20/40 and a mean age at onset of 42 years. The pattern was similar in the sporadic case in IMPG1 family 3, whose transmission was presumed to be recessive (age at onset, 38 years; mean visual acuity, 20/50). Nine of the 13 patients had drusen-like lesions next to the vitelliform deposits. On spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT), the vitelliform material lay above the RPE at every stage of the dystrophy, and the RPE was well preserved with its classical reflectivity. The vitelliform deposits were located between the ellipsoid and interdigitation lines. The EOG was normal or borderline in 9 patients. Meunier et al. (2014) noted that these features are not seen in the classical forms of BEST1- or PRPH2-related vitelliform dystrophy.

paragraphs.text: Brandl et al. (2017) described 2 sporadic VMD patients with IMPG1 mutations whose disease began in early childhood. The first patient, a boy from a German family, had reduced visual acuity at age 13 (0.2 logMAR in the right eye and 0.1 logMAR in the left eye). Both fundi showed central RPE abnormalities with foveal detachment. He was the only affected member of his family. The second patient was a boy from a consanguineous Turkish family. He was first diagnosed with VMD at age 2, and his visual acuity fluctuated around 0.2 logMAR in both eyes over 8 years of follow-up. At age 10, the multifocal electroretinogram (ERG) was normal and the EOG Arden ratio was borderline to slightly low. Each eye had a single central vitelliform lesion, and the lesion area enlarged during follow-up. SD-OCT showed a bilateral, central, dome-shaped foveal detachment of the neurosensory retina. The hyperreflective material beneath it was reabsorbed, leaving an optically empty cavity, and the photoreceptor outer segments were elongated. Bruch's membrane and the RPE kept their classical reflectivity. Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) showed circular hyperautofluorescence that lessened over time, and there were no satellite drusen. Brandl et al. (2017) commented that clinical symptoms tended to be more severe with IMPG1 mutations than with IMPG2 mutations.

paragraphs.text: Gupta et al. (2021) reported a 25-year-old woman with a symptomatic scotoma and decreased vision who had small yellow foveal spots in both eyes. Optical coherence tomography showed disorganization and reduced reflectance of the foveal ellipsoid and interdigitation zones, worse in the left eye than the right. FAF findings were minimal and dye angiography was unrevealing. The multifocal ERG showed slightly reduced retinal sensitivity in the central retina of the left eye.

paragraphs.text: Manes et al. (2013) studied a large family with autosomal dominant VMD using gene mapping and whole-exome sequencing. They identified a heterozygous c.713T-G mutation in the IMPG1 gene, resulting in a leu238-to-arg (L238R) substitution, and then found the same mutation in 2 other families with autosomal dominant VMD. Structural modeling predicted that the L238R substitution destabilizes the conserved SEA1 domain of SPACR, the protein encoded by IMPG1. Manes et al. (2013) then screened 144 probands with various forms of macular dystrophy and found 3 more IMPG1 mutations. Two affected members of a family with autosomal recessive VMD were homozygous for a splice site mutation (c.807+1G-T). Two affected members of another family were compound heterozygous for a leu154-to-pro (L154P) mutation and an arg507-to-ter (R507X) mutation.

paragraphs.text: Meunier et al. (2014) screened IMPG1 and IMPG2 in 49 families with vitelliform macular dystrophy who had no mutation, small deletion, or large rearrangement in BEST1 or PRPH2. They found IMPG1 mutations in 3 families (11 patients) and an IMPG2 mutation in 1 family. Two IMPG1 families had autosomal dominant transmission and carried the L238R mutation. In the third IMPG1 family, a sporadic case, transmission was presumed to be recessive. Overall, IMPG1 and IMPG2 accounted for 8% of the families without BEST1 or PRPH2 mutations.

paragraphs.text: Brandl et al. (2017) screened IMPG1 and IMPG2 in 106 unrelated patients with VMD who had no mutation in BEST1 or PRPH2. In 2 sporadic patients whose disease began in childhood, they found 2 novel IMPG1 mutations. The first patient was heterozygous for a c.713T-C mutation in exon 7, resulting in a leu238-to-pro (L238P) substitution in the SEA I domain. All 3 in silico tools predicted it to be pathogenic, and his parents could not be tested. The second patient, from a consanguineous Turkish family, was homozygous for a c.807+5G-A mutation in intron 7. Testing of the parents confirmed homozygosity, and both heterozygous parents were clinically unaffected. In an in vitro minigene splicing assay, the mutation caused exon 7 to be skipped in about half of the transcripts. Brandl et al. (2017) also found heterozygous IMPG2 mutations in 8 patients.

checks.explanation: The abstract states that the fish phenotype was consistent with the one seen in the families.

checks.claim: Medaka fish with morpholino knockdown of Impg1 and Impg2 had shortened rod and cone photoreceptor outer segments.
checks.evidence_quote: including a decreased length of rod and cone photoreceptor outer segments.
checks.explanation: 'Decreased length' of the outer segments means the same as 'shortened'.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a large family with autosomal dominant VMD4, Manes et al. (2013) used gene mapping and whole-exome sequencing to identify a heterozygous c.713T-G mutation in the IMPG1 gene, resulting in a leu238-to-arg (L238R) substitution. They found the same mutation in 2 other families with autosomal dominant VMD and the same phenotype. Structural modeling predicted that the substitution destabilizes the conserved SEA1 domain of SPACR.

checks.claim: Manes et al. (2013) used gene mapping and whole-exome sequencing to identify a heterozygous IMPG1 c.713T-G mutation, resulting in a leu238-to-arg (L238R) substitution, in affected members of a large family with autosomal dominant VMD4.
checks.evidence_quote: In a large family with autosomal-dominant VMD, gene mapping and whole-exome sequencing led to the identification of a c.713T>G (p.Leu238Arg) IMPG1 mutation
checks.explanation: Heterozygosity is implied by dominant inheritance.

checks.claim: Manes et al. (2013) found the IMPG1 L238R mutation in 2 other families with autosomal dominant VMD and the same phenotype.
checks.evidence_quote: which was subsequently found in two other families with autosomal-dominant VMD and the same phenotype

checks.claim: Structural modeling by Manes et al. (2013) predicted that the IMPG1 L238R substitution destabilizes the conserved SEA1 domain of SPACR.
checks.evidence_quote: Structural modeling indicates that the p.Leu238Arg substitution destabilizes the conserved SEA1 domain of SPACR.

paragraphs.text: Meunier et al. (2014) identified the L238R mutation in 2 families with autosomal dominant VMD4. Patients had late onset, moderate visual impairment, and drusen-like lesions next to the vitelliform deposits.

checks.claim: Meunier et al. (2014) identified the IMPG1 L238R mutation in 2 families with autosomal dominant VMD4.
checks.evidence_quote: With an autosomal dominant transmission, families 1 and 2 had the c.713T→G (p.Leu238Arg) mutation in IMPG1
checks.explanation: Stated; VMD4 is standard nomenclature for IMPG1-related VMD.

checks.claim: Patients with the IMPG1 L238R mutation reported by Meunier et al. (2014) had late onset.
checks.evidence_quote: Patients with IMPG1 or IMPG2 mutations had a late onset and moderate visual impairment (mean visual acuity, 20/40; mean age of onset, 42 years)
checks.explanation: The abstract reports late onset for all IMPG1 and IMPG2 patients together, not specifically for the L238R carriers.

checks.claim: Patients with the IMPG1 L238R mutation reported by Meunier et al. (2014) had moderate visual impairment.
checks.evidence_quote: Patients with IMPG1 or IMPG2 mutations had a late onset and moderate visual impairment
checks.explanation: Pooled finding across all IMPG1/IMPG2 patients, not specific to L238R families.

checks.claim: Patients with the IMPG1 L238R mutation reported by Meunier et al. (2014) had drusen-like lesions next to the vitelliform deposits.
checks.evidence_quote: Drusen-like lesions adjacent to the vitelliform deposits were observed in 9 of 13 patients.
checks.explanation: Seen in 9 of all 13 patients; the abstract does not say which mutation carriers had them, so attributing the finding to L238R patients is not specifically supported.

paragraphs.text: Manes et al. (2013) found a homozygous c.807+1G-T splice site mutation in the IMPG1 gene in 2 affected members of a family with autosomal recessive VMD4. The mutation was identified by screening 144 probands with various forms of macular dystrophy.

checks.claim: Manes et al. (2013) found a homozygous IMPG1 c.807+1G-T splice site mutation in 2 affected members of a family with autosomal recessive VMD4.
checks.evidence_quote: Two individuals from one family affected by autosomal-recessive VMD were homozygous for the splice-site mutation c.807+1G>T

checks.claim: Manes et al. (2013) identified the IMPG1 c.807+1G-T mutation by screening 144 probands with various forms of macular dystrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: Screening of 144 probands who had various forms of macular dystrophy revealed three other IMPG1 mutations. Two individuals from one family affected by autosomal-recessive VMD were homozygous for the splice-site mutation c.807+1G>T
checks.explanation: The splice mutation is one of the 3 mutations found in the screen.

paragraphs.text: Manes et al. (2013) found compound heterozygous mutations in the IMPG1 gene in 2 affected members of a family with VMD4: a c.461T-C transition, resulting in a leu154-to-pro (L154P) substitution, and a c.1519C-T transition, resulting in an arg507-to-ter (R507X) substitution.

checks.claim: Manes et al. (2013) found compound heterozygous IMPG1 mutations in 2 affected members of a family with VMD4.
checks.evidence_quote: two from another family were compound heterozygous for the mutations c.461T>C (p.Leu154Pro) and c.1519C>T (p.Arg507(∗))

checks.claim: One IMPG1 mutation found by Manes et al. (2013) in the compound heterozygous VMD4 family was a c.461T-C transition, resulting in a leu154-to-pro (L154P) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: compound heterozygous for the mutations c.461T>C (p.Leu154Pro)

checks.claim: The other IMPG1 mutation found by Manes et al. (2013) in the compound heterozygous VMD4 family was a c.1519C-T transition, resulting in an arg507-to-ter (R507X) substitution.

paragraphs.text: Gupta et al. (2021) found a heterozygous L154P mutation in the IMPG1 gene in a 25-year-old woman with a symptomatic scotoma, decreased vision, small yellow foveal spots in both eyes, and disorganization of the foveal ellipsoid and interdigitation zones. They suggested that the mutation may cause symptomatic outer retinal disturbance in the heterozygous state.

checks.claim: Gupta et al. (2021) found a heterozygous IMPG1 L154P mutation in a 25-year-old woman with a symptomatic scotoma and decreased vision.
checks.evidence_quote: We describe a case of a 25-year-old female patient with symptomatic scotoma and vision decrease
checks.explanation: The abstract also states that genetic testing found a heterozygous p.Leu154Pro mutation in IMPG1.

checks.claim: The 25-year-old woman with the heterozygous IMPG1 L154P mutation reported by Gupta et al. (2021) had small yellow foveal spots in both eyes.
checks.evidence_quote: who exhibited bilateral small foveal yellow spots

checks.claim: The 25-year-old woman with the heterozygous IMPG1 L154P mutation reported by Gupta et al. (2021) had disorganization of the foveal ellipsoid and interdigitation zones.
checks.evidence_quote: Optical coherence tomography revealed disorganization and decreased reflectance of the foveal ellipsoid and interdigitation zones

checks.claim: Gupta et al. (2021) suggested that the IMPG1 L154P mutation may cause symptomatic outer retinal disturbance in the heterozygous state.
checks.evidence_quote: The p.Leu154Pro IMPG1 mutation may cause symptomatic outer retinal disturbance in the heterozygous state.

paragraphs.text: For discussion of the c.1519C-T transition in the IMPG1 gene, resulting in an arg507-to-ter (R507X) substitution, which Manes et al. (2013) found in compound heterozygous state with L154P in 2 affected members of a family with VMD4, see IMPG1, LEU154PRO.

checks.claim: Manes et al. (2013) found the IMPG1 c.1519C-T transition, resulting in an arg507-to-ter (R507X) substitution, in compound heterozygous state with L154P in 2 affected members of a family with VMD4.
checks.evidence_quote: two from another family were compound heterozygous for the mutations c.461T>C (p.Leu154Pro) and c.1519C>T (p.Arg507(∗))

paragraphs.text: In a sporadic German boy with VMD4 and reduced visual acuity at age 13, Brandl et al. (2017) identified a heterozygous c.713T-C transition in exon 7 of the IMPG1 gene, resulting in a leu238-to-pro (L238P) substitution in the SEA I domain. The mutation was found by next-generation sequencing and confirmed by Sanger sequencing, and all 3 in silico tools predicted it to be pathogenic. His parents were not available for testing. The same codon is affected by the L238R mutation.

checks.claim: Brandl et al. (2017) identified a heterozygous IMPG1 c.713T-C transition in exon 7, resulting in a leu238-to-pro (L238P) substitution in the SEA I domain, in a sporadic German boy with VMD4.
checks.evidence_quote: Patient #1 of the German family 13-501 carries a heterozygous c.713T > C nucleotide change in exon 7 of the IMPG1 gene that leads to a p.(Leu238Pro) amino acid substitution in the SEA I domain

checks.claim: The German boy with the IMPG1 L238P mutation reported by Brandl et al. (2017) had reduced visual acuity at age 13.
checks.evidence_quote: At the age of 13, patient #1 showed reduced visual acuity

checks.claim: The IMPG1 L238P mutation was found by next-generation sequencing and confirmed by Sanger sequencing.
checks.evidence_quote: Potentially disease-relevant variants were confirmed by Sanger chain-terminating dideoxynucleotide sequencing.
checks.explanation: The Methods section describes NGS screening followed by Sanger confirmation.

checks.claim: All 3 in silico tools used by Brandl et al. (2017) predicted the IMPG1 L238P mutation to be pathogenic.
checks.evidence_quote: is predicted to be pathogenic by all three algorithms used in the in silico analysis

checks.claim: The parents of the German boy with the IMPG1 L238P mutation were not available for testing.
checks.evidence_quote: Data on ophthalmological examination or genetic testing of the parents of patient #1 were not available.

checks.claim: The IMPG1 L238P mutation affects the same codon as the IMPG1 L238R mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: Both mutations lead to the substitution of the moderately conserved, hydrophobic amino acid leucine at position 238 to either a positively charged arginine [p.(Leu238Arg)] or to a cyclic proline [p.(Leu238Pro)].

paragraphs.text: In a boy from a consanguineous Turkish family who was diagnosed with VMD4 at age 2, Brandl et al. (2017) identified a homozygous c.807+5G-A transition in intron 7 of the IMPG1 gene. Homozygosity was confirmed by testing the parents, and both heterozygous parents, aged 35 and 40 years, were clinically unaffected. In an in vitro minigene splicing assay in HEK293 cells, the mutation caused exon 7 to be skipped in about half of the transcripts.

checks.claim: Brandl et al. (2017) identified a homozygous IMPG1 c.807+5G-A transition in intron 7 in a boy from a consanguineous Turkish family.
checks.evidence_quote: a c.807 + 5G > A mutation in intron 7 causing aberrant splicing of the IMPG1 mRNA, was found in a young Turkish boy in a homozygous state

checks.claim: The Turkish boy with the homozygous IMPG1 c.807+5G-A mutation was diagnosed with VMD4 at age 2.
checks.evidence_quote: Patient #2 was initially diagnosed with vitelliform macular dystrophy at the age of 2

checks.claim: Homozygosity for the IMPG1 c.807+5G-A mutation in the Turkish boy was confirmed by testing the parents.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygosity was confirmed by segregation analysis in the genomic DNA of the parents.

checks.claim: Both parents of the Turkish boy, aged 35 and 40 years, were heterozygous for the IMPG1 c.807+5G-A mutation and clinically unaffected.
checks.evidence_quote: Both heterozygous 35- and 40-year-old parents of patient #2 are clinically asymptomatic with full visual acuity and regular findings in multimodal retinal imaging

checks.claim: In an in vitro minigene splicing assay in HEK293 cells, the IMPG1 c.807+5G-A mutation caused exon 7 to be skipped in about half of the transcripts.
checks.evidence_quote: The analysis of cDNA derived from HEK293 cells transfected with a construct containing the c.807 + 5G > A mutation, revealed aberrant pre-mRNA splicing; exon 7 was skipped in about half of the transcripts
